classroom.title: Class Workspace
classroom.description: Use Class Workspace to organize course recordings and share folders. Instructors can also review the roster and Listening Guy conversations attached to course work.

export-and-sharing.title: Export & Sharing
export-and-sharing.description: Download audio, make a public listening link, or share course recordings through a folder. Choose the option that matches who needs access.

getting-started.title: Getting Started
getting-started.description: Sign in, choose a familiar recording, and make your first split. Knowing the song will help you compare the separated parts with the full mix.

index.title: Stem Splitter Documentation
index.description: Separate a recording into musical parts, compare them in the mixer, and pin notes to the moments you want to discuss.

instructor-console.title: Instructor Console
instructor-console.description: Set the vocabulary and listening tasks you want Listening Guy to use. Give it instructions students can test with the mixer.

listening-guy.title: Listening Guy
listening-guy.description: Ask about a recording, try the suggested mixer action, and check the answer by listening. Listening Guy can control the mixer, but it cannot hear the audio.

live-sessions.title: Live Sessions
live-sessions.description: Lead playback from your mixer while students follow on their own devices. Headphones let each student hear the shared passage and set their own volume.

mixer.title: The Mixer
mixer.description: Hear one part alone, compare it with the full mix, or repeat a passage until you can describe what changed.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Pin a comment to a moment in the recording so the next listener can find the passage and check your description.

privacy-and-limits.title: Privacy & Limits
privacy-and-limits.description: Personal work is private to your account. Course work permits instructor review after you acknowledge the policy; classmates need access through a shared folder.

sample-activities.title: Sample Activities
sample-activities.description: Try these short listening tasks with a recording your class is using. Each moves from a mixer action to a note about what students heard.

splitter-basics.title: Splitter Basics
splitter-basics.description: Find your recording in the Session Rack, open its mixer, and use the surrounding controls to manage your work.

student-onboarding.title: Student Onboarding
student-onboarding.description: Start with a prepared recording so students can learn the mixer and save a note before importing their own audio.

teaching-tips.title: Teaching Tips
teaching-tips.description: Ask students to describe a sound before naming the musical concept. Use one mixer change at a time so they can hear what makes the difference.

use-cases.title: Use Cases
use-cases.description: Start with a recording, describe what you hear, and compare the full mix with isolated parts. Use notes to show where your account comes from.

course-access.title: Course Access
course-access.description: Enter your course workspace through the Lab and keep its maps separate from your other projects.

evidence-and-field-notes.title: Evidence & Field Notes
evidence-and-field-notes.description: Show which passage supports a claim, explain your reading, and use Field Notes to guide your next inquiry.

export-and-sharing.title: Export & Sharing
export-and-sharing.description: Share a live project link or an exported copy, and record a saved course revision when your instructor asks.

getting-started.title: Getting Started
getting-started.description: Accept your course invitation, open a project, and build a first Micro map from one memo.

index.title: Systems Mapping Documentation
index.description: Build a map from a case or fieldwork memo, and show how each claim follows from the evidence.

instructor-console.title: Instructor Console
instructor-console.description: Give students a question for each level and follow their progress while keeping private map content separate.

levels.title: The Four Levels
levels.description: Follow the focal person's direct encounters, relationships between mapped items, outside decisions, and broader conditions across one cumulative map.

map.title: The Map
map.description: Place items where the case supports them, then describe the relationships a reader should follow.

memo-and-suggestions.title: Memo & Suggestions
memo-and-suggestions.description: Compare each model suggestion with your memo before deciding what belongs on the map.

privacy-and-limits.title: Privacy & Limits
privacy-and-limits.description: Check who can read your work and what leaves the browser before you add a memo or share a map.

sample-activities.title: Sample Activities
sample-activities.description: Give students a short mapping task that asks them to inspect a source, make a choice, and explain it.

student-onboarding.title: Student Onboarding
student-onboarding.description: Use one shared case during the first week so you can help students reach a saved Micro map.

teaching-tips.title: Teaching Tips
teaching-tips.description: Use each level to ask students where a claim belongs and which passage supports it.

use-cases.title: Use Cases
use-cases.description: Adapt a shared case, a community inquiry, or field-placement notes into a sequence of mapping assignments.

workspace-basics.title: Workspace Basics
workspace-basics.description: Move between the map and your writing without losing your place in either.
